issues: Overclaim about what is included in semi-annual Board climate risk reporting (financial impacts and management actions) versus what is evidenced (register contains those fields; Board reporting frequency is evidenced, but pack content is not).
Some committee-activity/process descriptions are more detailed than the compact evidence supports (beyond meeting frequency and the documented decisions list).
A few broad governance/control phrases imply wider structures (control functions; governance KPIs framework) than evidenced.
available_evidence_omitted: Governance alignment flags (TCFD-aligned=true; IFRS S2-aligned=true) are not disclosed anywhere (they are available, but if used must be framed as internal indicators and not as assured/controlled alignment).

Board-level ERM integration flag is stated only indirectly via the risk-register linkage count; the explicit governance-level ERM integration flag (erm_integration_flag=true) is not clearly stated as a governance control/connection.
unsupported_claims: “Through this reporting, the Board is informed about … associated financial impacts and related management actions.” (financial impacts and management actions are evidenced at risk-register level, but it is not evidenced that the Board pack includes financial impact quantification and management actions, nor that the Board is informed of those specific elements).

“The committee’s work in 2024 included reviewing management proposals … considering progress … discussing … indicators.” (plausible but not directly evidenced beyond meeting frequency and the existence of documented decisions; reads as process detail not anchored to the compact decision evidence).

“These decisions show … resource allocation (including carbon credit procurement) … and the integration of climate-related metrics into executive remuneration.” (the decisions evidence includes discussion of remuneration ESG KPIs, but “integration” is stronger than evidenced; also “resource allocation” is an interpretation rather than a stated governance control).

“The Bank has a skills development programme that relates to climate-related risks and opportunities.” (skills_development_programme=true supports existence, but the draft implies scope/content ‘relates to climate-related risks and opportunities’ without detail; acceptable if kept high-level but currently reads as more specific than evidenced).
material_unsupported_claims: Board reporting content overclaim: statements implying the semi-annual Board climate risk reporting includes quantified financial impacts and management actions (not evidenced as Board-report content; only evidenced that the register contains financial impacts and mitigation actions).
minor_wording_to_tighten: “organises climate-related governance across … control functions” (control functions are not evidenced in the compact governance evidence; either name the evidenced bodies only or clarify at a high level without implying specific control-function roles).
“governance key performance indicators” (the metrics are evidenced, but calling them governance KPIs may imply a formal KPI framework; consider “governance indicators we track/disclose”).

Risk-register mitigation action mapping: several material risk examples show mitigation actions that do not logically match the named risk (e.g., stranded assets risk paired with flood mapping overlay). This may be a data-quality artefact, but in narrative it reads like an asserted control design; consider describing mitigation actions as examples across the register rather than attaching them to specific risks unless validated.
correctly_disclosed_evidence_boundaries: No separate climate-specific charter/terms of reference for the ESG & Sustainability Committee is disclosed.
No quantified/specific Board-level trade-offs are disclosed in decision records; therefore no trade-off analysis is presented.
No formal process for assessing adequacy of Board climate skills against defined criteria is disclosed.
No formal escalation thresholds/trigger-based escalation mechanics are disclosed.
Management committee naming differs across years; the report does not infer continuity/renaming.
No separate governance control process to verify/assure TCFD/IFRS S2 alignment is disclosed (boundary stated).
Climate checks for major transactions are described without claiming a mandatory policy across all transactions.
Assurance scope is clearly limited to Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions; financed emissions are outside scope.
